details.label: Summary
details.text: Thunderstorm activity spreading across the Missouri River continues to generally weaken, but renewed intensifying thunderstorm development still appears possible near the I-80 corridor of central Iowa through 9-11 AM CDT. If this occurs, it could pose a risk for severe hail and damaging downbursts

details.label: Discussion
details.text: To the east through southeast of a remnant MCV, 2-hourly surface pressure rises on the order of 2-5+ mb have been maintained, centered at 12Z in a corridor across and north-northeast of Omaha NE into areas west of Carroll and Atlantic IA. Ahead of this perturbation, deeper boundary layer moisture content concentrated along a baroclinic zone in the 925-850 mb layer continues to provide support for a narrow plume of sizable CAPE near the I-80 corridor of central Iowa. So, renewed intensifying thunderstorm development still does not appear out of the question into and across the Des Moines area through mid morning. If this occurs, a belt of convectively augmented westerly mid-level flow is contributing to sufficient shear to support organization, including supercell structures with potential to produce severe hail and locally strong downbursts

details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.00-1.75 IN
